thread:
kai: Kicking off a short thread to lock down a lightweight 'MatchBench' protocol for one-to-one model comparisons. Scope: same prompts, tokenizer alignment, identical decoding params, stop sequences, and explicit runtime knobs (kernels, batching, KV cache warm state). Need this nailed before the next perf run. :eyes:
amy: +1. Biggest sources of nondeterminism I've seen: different tokenizer special-token handling (BOS/EOS), whitespace normalization, and stop-seq semantics across decoders. We should canonicalize preproc and postproc. :thumbsup:
raj: Agree. Also need to pin kernel selection and quantization path. Proposal: force kernel policy to 'exact' so both variants use the same execution path for apples-to-apples. Example env: `REDWOOD_KERNEL_POLICY=exact` and `FORCE_QUANT_MODE=none` during the comparison.
marta: Suggest a concrete harness command for the replay harness so everyone runs the same thing. My draft:
```
./replay_harness --log-level=info \
  --model v1.2.0 --seed 42 \
  --tokenizer-canonical=plain_text --tokenizer-normalize=spaces \
  --decode-mode=greedy --max-tokens=128 --stop-seqs='["\\n\\n","###"]' \
  --kernel-policy=exact --force-quant=none \
  --batching-window-ms=10 --max-batch=16 \
  --kv-cache=warm --warm-prefix=2000
```
We should keep `seed` and `tokenizer-canonical` required fields.
amy: Love it. Two small requests: 1) add `--tokenizer-vocab-check` to validate token counts before run; 2) include an output sanity check that verifies stop sequences didn't leak tokens (postproc trim).
kai: Good call. Also we need to document two cache states: cold and warm. For warm, use the same prefix-length (e.g., 2000 tokens from replay) and for cold, flush KV and run zero-prefix. We'll run both and publish delta.
raj: On batching heuristics: run at two windows: 10ms (low latency) and 50ms (throughput). Record both p50/p95 latencies and per-token cost. Use the same request arrival pattern from the replay to keep request-size distribution identical.
perf-bot: quick profiling snippet from today's smoke run (trimmed):
```
[PROFILE] model=v1.2.0 kernel=attn_fused fp16
[PROFILE] seq=128 batch=8 tokens/sec=12.3 latency_per_token_ms=2.8
[kv] warm_hit_ratio=0.83 evictions=0
[kernel-switch] chosen=attn_fused fallback=attn_generic
```
marta: That `kernel-switch` line is interesting — shows runtime may still pick a fallback when memory layout differs. We must ensure memory layout is identical (same batch shapes, same padding strategy). So add `--pad-strategy=right` to the canonical cmd.
ops-bot: Note: for Dedicated runs, set `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_OVERRIDE=deterministic` to avoid autoscale-induced node churn during the run.
amy: For tokenizer alignment test, include a small unit: feed the same prompt into both tokenizers and assert token ids equal and length equal. Example python check:
```
ids_a = tok_a.encode(prompt)
ids_b = tok_b.encode(prompt)
assert ids_a == ids_b, 'tokenizer mismatch' 
```
If mismatch, abort the comparison and log diffs.
kai: Good. Also capture a short canonical metadata JSON for each run (model, kernel policy, quant, tokenizer hash, decode params, kv_state, batching window). We'll attach that to metrics.
raj: One more edge case: stop sequences that are substrings of tokens (e.g., '###' vs token boundaries). We should run two variants: stop-by-token and stop-by-string, and prefer token-based if both tokenizers align. Document which was used.
marta: I'll own writing the MatchBench README and the harness wrapper that sets all these flags and performs the tokenizer checks. Target: PR by EOD Wednesday.
kai: Thanks. Action items: marta PR for harness + README; amy add tokenizer-vocab-check and postproc sanity; raj run kernel/quantization forced runs and upload profiling; I'll coordinate scheduling and combine the cold/warm runs.
perf-bot: Scheduled: matchbench-run-190128 (cold + warm + two batching windows) queued on 2025-06-11 09:00:00 UTC.
kai: Perfect. If anyone has additional gotchas, drop them here. Otherwise we'll standardize this as the default for one-to-one parity checks. :rocket:
